Attain

/uh-TAYN/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Attain means to succeed in achieving something through effort.

After four years of night classes, Rafael finally attained his engineering license.

Worked Example

The cellist had failed the conservatory audition twice. Between attempts she practiced four hours before work and two after, recording herself and fixing one flaw a week. She spent her savings on a summer intensive and played in every free recital that would have her. On the third audition, the panel stopped her halfway through the concerto — to offer her the seat on the spot. At twenty-six, she had attained the position she had chased since childhood.

The cellist reaches her goal only through years of effort and repeated attempts — success earned by work, which is exactly what attain means.

How Attain Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

achieve

achieve: to reach a goal through effort

reach

reach: to arrive at

Antonyms

forfeit

forfeit: to lose by one's own failure

miss

miss: to fail to reach

How Strong Is It? — reach → attain → conquer

reach vs. attain

reach vs. attain: Reach is plainer and weaker — you can reach a shelf or a bus stop; to attain something is to arrive at a prized goal through real effort.

conquer vs. attain

conquer vs. attain: Conquer is stronger than attain: it adds the drama of defeating resistance entirely, while attain quietly credits the work behind the success.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — at-

Prefix — at-: toward (from Latin ad-)

Root — tain

Root — tain: to touch (Latin tangere, via Old French ataindre)

Put it together

Put it together: Attain comes through Old French ataindre from Latin attingere: ad- (toward) plus tangere (to touch). To attain a goal is literally to reach out and finally touch it. The touching root tangere leaves fingerprints all over English — contact (touching together), tangible (touchable), intact (untouched).

Use the root in a new word: intact

Use the root in a new word: intact: The seal on the jar was still intact — intact literally means 'untouched,' from the same Latin tangere (to touch) that lets attain mean finally touching the goal you reached for.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal; goals, ranks, levels ('attain mastery', 'attain the rank of')

Attain always implies effort behind the arrival — you attain a rank, a degree, a level of skill. Things that come to you by luck, gift, or birth are received or inherited, not attained.
